To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the future HR executives in Hong kong need a set of core competencies that include the following: (1) a strategic orientation; (2) business and industry knowledge; (3) a global perspective; (4) a strong analytical and conceptual capability; and (5) the ability to work in a cross-functional team.

the HR executives and CEOs agree on the need to develop the following competencies for future HR executives: 1) Strategic thinking and planning, 2) Business and financial acumen, 3) Communication and presentation skills, 4) Change management and organizational development, 5) People management and leadership, 6) Information technology, 7) Knowledge management, 8) Globalization, 9) Ethics, 10) Legal compliance, 11) Employee relations, 12)
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the key competencies required of future HR executives in Hong Kng.
the identification of the key human resources competencies that are required in the future.
the identification of the competencies required for future HR leaders, in order to develop a framework for developing the HR executives in HongKong.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CEOs and HR executives in this study agree that HR executives in Hongkong should have a high level of competencies in strategic thinking and business knowledge, and a moderate level of competencies for other HR related competencies, such as leadership and interpersonal skills.
the CEOs and HR executives agreed that HR executives should be equipped with a broad range of competencies.

HR practitioners need to have a good understanding of business and the ability to contribute to business strategies, and that HR executives should be able to provide a strategic view of the organization and the ability to influence the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HR leaders in Hong kong should be able to understand the business environment and the business strategy, and to translate business strategy into HR strategy.

the HR executives are not well equipped to meet the demands of the business environment and that there is a gap between the views of CEOs regarding the required competencies of HR leaders and those of the HR executives themselves.

the HR executives in Hongkong should be equipped with the following 6 competencies: business knowledge, business strategy and leadership, change management, HR knowledge and skills, HR strategic thinking and HR technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HR profession in Hong Kong needs to be transformed from a technical and administrative support function into a strategic and value-adding business partner function.
HR executives should develop their competencies to be a business partner and a strategist in a business.
CEOs and HR executives in Hong Hong share a common view of what HR executives should be.
